title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
authors: Victor Sanh, Lysandre Debut, Julien Chaumond, Thomas Wolf

pages.title: A smaller BERT that keeps 97% of its quality

blocks.html: BERT-Base is 110M parameters and runs slowly enough that real-time, on-device, and high-throughput deployments often can't use it. DistilBERT compresses BERT-Base by 40% (to ~66M parameters), runs 60% faster, and retains 97% of BERT's language understanding capabilities on GLUE.

The technique is knowledge distillation (Hinton et al.): train a smaller 'student' model to mimic a larger 'teacher.' Applied here at the pre-training stage, not just at fine-tuning — which is the key contribution.

Start with BERT-Base (12 layers, 12 heads, hidden 768). DistilBERT keeps the same hidden dimension and number of heads but halves the number of layers to 6. Token-type embeddings and the pooler are removed (rarely used downstream). The student is initialized by taking every other layer of the teacher.

items: Distillation loss $\mathcal{L}_{\text{ce}}$: cross-entropy between the student's and teacher's softmax outputs over the masked tokens, with a temperature $T$ to soften both distributions. The student learns the teacher's distribution over the vocabulary, not just the argmax — much more information per training example than hard labels.
Masked LM loss $\mathcal{L}_{\text{mlm}}$: the standard BERT MLM objective, using ground-truth tokens.
Cosine embedding loss $\mathcal{L}_{\text{cos}}$: align the directions of student and teacher hidden states. Helps the student match the teacher's internal representations, not just outputs.

blocks.html: On GLUE (9 NLU benchmarks averaged), DistilBERT scores 77.0 vs BERT-Base's 79.5 — a 2.5 point gap, or 97% of BERT's score retained.
Inference: 60% faster than BERT-Base on a single CPU; even larger speedup on mobile. Memory footprint shrinks from ~440MB to ~250MB.
On SQuAD 1.1, DistilBERT gets F1 86.2 vs BERT-Base's 88.5 — within 2.3 points. After task-specific fine-tuning with another distillation step on top, the gap narrows further.

DistilBERT was an inflection point for practical NLP deployments. It made BERT-class quality accessible at edge-device latencies and budgets, and established knowledge distillation as a first-class compression technique for Transformers.

Direct descendants and analogs: TinyBERT, MobileBERT, MiniLM, ALBERT (a different compression approach via parameter sharing), and the modern wave of distilled instruction-tuned models (DistilGPT-2, Alpaca's distillation-from-GPT-3.5 lineage, Llama-distillation methods).
